evidence.label: mcp-js-prototype-pollution-merge-loop (medium/medium)
evidence.detail: Keys from a caller-supplied object are copied onto a target without excluding __proto__ / constructor / prototype. A tool argument carrying __proto__ then mutates Object.prototype for the whole process, which can turn an unrelated later property read into attacker-controlled data.

evidence.label: authentication_model
evidence.detail: registry declares credential header(s) Authorization that are not required on every declared endpoint, and the source we fetched shows no enforcement — `03` §4's "authentication present but optional" band; 1 of 1 declared remote endpoint(s) require no credential header: https://mcp.mux.com

evidence.label: transport_security
evidence.detail: declared endpoint(s) are HTTPS: https://mcp.mux.com; scored 80, not 100: `03` §4 reserves 100 for HTTPS *with HSTS*, and an HSTS header can only be seen by connecting, which `04` §9 does not do. This is an unverifiable band, not an observed absence.

evidence.label: secret_handling
evidence.detail: detect-secrets matched 3 credential-shaped string(s), every one from a keyword or entropy heuristic (Secret Keyword). Those flag placeholders, variable names and content hashes as readily as credentials, so they do not establish the committed credential `03` §4's 0 asserts, and this sub-check is not scored; Secret Keyword at README.md:21; Secret Keyword at README.md:22; Secret Keyword at README.md:24

evidence.label: authorization_granularity
evidence.detail: no tool registration was recognised anywhere in the source. An MCP server registers tools by definition, so this is a gap in our detection rather than a server with none, and `03` §4's threshold cannot be applied to it.

evidence.label: recency
evidence.detail: last commit 7 day(s) before 2026-11-18

evidence.label: issue_responsiveness
evidence.detail: only 2 issue(s) from outside the project fall inside `03` §5's 6-month window, which is under §5's floor of 3, and §5's lifetime-median fallback needs this repository's whole issue history — more of it than `04` §7's bounded fetch reads. A limit of ours, not a finding about the server.

evidence.label: release_cadence
evidence.detail: released 7 day(s) ago (by releases), inside `03` §5's 30-day window

evidence.label: bus_factor
evidence.detail: sole maintainer

evidence.label: repository_signals
evidence.detail: `03` §5 scores this by quartile WITHIN the server's category, which needs a distribution across every scanned server and so cannot be computed while scanning one. It is a post-pass over the crawl and that pass does not exist yet.

dependency_health.reason: no lockfile in the published package (npm does not publish a package's package-lock.json; npm-shrinkwrap.json is the lockfile a published package can carry); dependency versions are unresolved, so no vulnerability can be attributed

evidence.label: license
evidence.detail: LICENSE present with no SPDX-License-Identifier tag; identified as 'Apache-2.0' from its text

evidence.label: readme_quality
evidence.detail: README.md: installation instructions (+25), configuration documented (+25), exposed tools or resources enumerated (+30), states what the server does in the first 200 words (+20)

evidence.label: declared_scopes
evidence.detail: neither the README nor the MCP manifest documents what the server accesses or what side effects it has

evidence.label: changelog
evidence.detail: no CHANGELOG in the fetched source. `03` §7's partial credit for tagged releases carrying release notes is not applied here — that needs the forge API, which this check does not call

evidence.label: security_contact
evidence.detail: no SECURITY.md and no disclosure contact in the README, so a finder has no route to report a vulnerability privately

install_resolution.label: Resolved by deps.dev, not read from a lockfile the publisher shipped: these are the versions deps.dev's resolver picked for an install of this package, which can differ from what a real install picks. deps.dev records no resolution time and has been measured lagging the npm registry by up to about 30 hours. Listed only — nothing here changes a score. Data: deps.dev (Open Source Insights), CC BY 4.0.
